pause_and_think.prompt: Which phase comes right after the period?
pause_and_think.explanation: After the period, the follicular phase begins and a new egg starts growing in the ovary.

pause_and_think.prompt: Which hormone helps build the cosy lining?
pause_and_think.explanation: Oestrogen rises in the first half and builds the lining. Progesterone keeps it ready in the second half.

pause_and_think.prompt: For most teens, how long is one cycle?
pause_and_think.explanation: For teens, 21 to 45 days is common while the body finds its rhythm.

discover_cards.label: SCIENCE FACT
discover_cards.front: A girl is born with all the eggs she will ever have.
discover_cards.back: That’s about 1 to 2 million at birth! Only around 400 are ever released in a lifetime.

discover_cards.label: MYTH OR FACT?
discover_cards.front: “You shouldn’t exercise or play during your period.”
discover_cards.back: Gentle movement often eases cramps. Dance, play, stretch, whatever feels good for you.

discover_cards.label: GIGI WONDERS
discover_cards.front: Why is it called a cycle?
discover_cards.back: Because it goes round and round and starts again, a bit like the moon’s phases. That’s why your Play activity was a moon!

reflect.journal_prompt: Before today I thought periods were… Now I know…

quick_check.prompt: The period is when…
quick_check.explanation: Yes, the lining gently leaves the body. That’s day 1 of a new cycle.

quick_check.prompt: Every girl’s cycle is exactly 28 days.
quick_check.explanation: False! Cycles vary, especially in the first couple of years.

quick_check.prompt: Which phase comes right after the egg is released?
quick_check.explanation: The luteal phase: the lining waits, just in case.

reflect.summary: 3 things you know now: periods are part of a cycle, cycles vary, and tracking helps.

discover_cards.label: SCIENCE FACT

discover_cards.label: SCIENCE FACT
discover_cards.front: POCSO stands for Protection of Children from Sexual Offences.
discover_cards.back: It became law in India in 2012 to keep children safe.

discover_cards.label: MYTH OR FACT?
discover_cards.front: “Only the police can report abuse.”
discover_cards.back: Anyone can report, including a child, a parent or a teacher.

discover_cards.label: GIGI WONDERS
discover_cards.front: What is 1098?
discover_cards.back: It’s India’s free Child Helpline, open day and night. Anyone can call for a child who needs help.

topics.title: What makes a good friend?
topics.caption: Good friends are kind, honest and respect your choices.

topics.title: Speak up: being assertive
topics.caption: Say what you need, calmly and clearly: “I feel… when… I need…”

topics.title: Handling disagreements kindly
topics.caption: Cool down, listen, find a fix together.

topics.title: Self-esteem: liking who you are
topics.caption: You are more than your looks or your marks.

discover_cards.label: SCIENCE FACT
discover_cards.front: Starting with “I feel” helps people listen instead of argue.
discover_cards.back: “I” messages share your feelings without blaming, so the other person doesn’t feel attacked.

discover_cards.label: MYTH OR FACT?
discover_cards.front: “Good friends never fight.”
discover_cards.back: Even best friends disagree. What matters is how you sort it out.

discover_cards.label: GIGI WONDERS
discover_cards.front: How do I say no without losing a friend?
discover_cards.back: “No thanks, but let’s do something else together.” Real friends respect a no.

topics.caption: When you name a feeling, it gets a little smaller.

topics.caption: Breathe, move, talk, write. Find what works for you.

topics.title: Empathy: feeling with others
topics.caption: Imagine how someone else feels, and be kind.

topics.title: Bouncing back from setbacks
topics.caption: Mistakes help you grow. Try again, a little differently.

discover_cards.label: SCIENCE FACT
discover_cards.front: Breathing out slowly tells your body it’s safe.
discover_cards.back: Long out-breaths slow your heartbeat and calm your nerves within a minute.

discover_cards.label: MYTH OR FACT?
discover_cards.front: “Strong girls don’t cry.”
discover_cards.back: Crying is a healthy way to let feelings out. Brave people feel things too.

discover_cards.label: GIGI WONDERS
discover_cards.front: What if I feel sad for a long time?
discover_cards.back: If sadness stays for weeks, tell a trusted adult or a counsellor. Asking for help is strong.
